aboutprojectpage.3841022721: “The traditional school focuses on academic theory, while the modern world requires applied skills, developed design thinking and the ability to work in cross-cultural teams. »
aboutprojectpage.d1728b4c: Do you want to become part of the international community?
aboutprojectpage.ac15bd8cf7: We are creating the future of education by connecting active students, academic mentors and global companies into a single, supportive development ecosystem.
aboutprojectpage.05c82da787: Navykus was created as a bridge between school desks and real professional challenges. We believe that every student, regardless of geographic location, deserves access to world-class mentoring, cutting-edge design tools, and a global community of like-minded people.
aboutprojectpage.c2b671bade: Our community brings together guys from more than 15 countries, speaking different languages, but united by one passion - creating viable projects that change the world for the better.
aboutprojectpage.4d60e65bd8: Navykus is not just an educational site. It is an international launching pad, breaking down boundaries and creating a new generation of conscious leaders.
aboutprojectpage.31f9f3d409: Navykus brings together key participants in the educational ecosystem. Select your role to discover the benefits and take the first step towards collaboration.
aboutprojectpage.b23f0c7c43: What can you do at Navykus
aboutprojectpage.d5362b6b2b: The platform provides a continuous development cycle - from the first idea to the presentation of a working MVP.
aboutprojectpage.e6970f04e8: We have collected the most frequently asked questions from parents, students and mentors.

aboutprojectpage.cc18b5c571: Implementation of corporate social responsibility initiatives
aboutprojectpage.9d86488fb6: Solve global cases in the field of ecology, urbanism, IT and diplomacy. Compete with students from other countries for grants and recognition.
aboutprojectpage.9915e585a3: Transform your bold ideas into working prototypes and startups using proven methods from the world's leading incubators.
aboutprojectpage.66695efbd6: Use our smart matching system to find collaborators, designers, coders, or join a promising initiative.
aboutprojectpage.c22bfce55b: Pitch your ideas to experts from MIT, Y Combinator, and leading corporations. High-quality feedback accelerates growth significantly.
aboutprojectpage.48d877aa9c: Attend webinars, master classes and workshops on programming, pitching, analytics and design absolutely free.
aboutprojectpage.20a478bc7a: Master critical thinking, systems approach, digital literacy and emotional intelligence in an applied format.
aboutprojectpage.4b5e0f1908: Who can become a participant in the project?
aboutprojectpage.09fd377d38: The project was created for active schoolchildren and students aged 10 to 22 years old who are interested in project activities, startups, technology, social innovation and international communication.
aboutprojectpage.a4f04e2aad: Is prior experience in hackathons required?
aboutprojectpage.3aeea8f6e3: Absolutely not! Our championships and programs are structured in such a way that they are comfortable for beginners to enter. Team trackers and webinars will help you master the basic design logic from scratch.
aboutprojectpage.ace0eadb3d: Can I submit a questionnaire if I do not have a team?
aboutprojectpage.090808a2de: Yes. Add your interests, skills, and roles to the questionnaire. After moderation, it will appear in Find a team.
aboutprojectpage.1d5cd942b3: How does the team search process work?
aboutprojectpage.3e6cba422a: Search the questionnaire catalog and filter participants by skills, roles, and interests.
aboutprojectpage.55cd784afe: How do events and project defense work?
aboutprojectpage.b38dd282f8: All processes take place entirely online on our platform. Workshops and lectures are broadcast recorded and live, work is carried out in Miro/Figma, and projects are defended in front of a jury in Zoom or Discord.
aboutprojectpage.e663d62bb5: How can I contact the organizers of Navykus?
aboutprojectpage.b966ab17f5: Write to info@navykus.tech. We will answer organizational and technical questions.

privacypolicy.title: Privacy Policy of the Navykus Project

blocks: p|This Privacy Policy of the Navykus project (hereinafter — the **Policy**) defines the procedure for processing and protecting personal data of individuals provided when using the website **{{siteUrl}}** (hereinafter — the **Website**), as well as when participating in championships, case championships, events, workshops and other Navykus project activities.
p|Navykus is an international educational platform for school students and young people aged 10 to 22.

p|This Policy has been drafted taking into account the provisions of the legislation of the Russian Federation on personal data, including Federal Law No. 152-FZ of 27.07.2006 "On Personal Data", as well as, where applicable, the requirements of the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).
p|The personal data operator is an individual — **{{operatorName}}**, operating as a sole proprietor (self-employed).
p|Operator details:

list|TIN: **{{operatorInn}}**
OGRNIP: **{{operatorOgrnip}}**
address: **{{operatorAddress}}**
entry in the personal data operators register: No. **{{operatorRegistryNumber}}** dated **{{operatorRegistryDate}}**
p|The Operator processes personal data for the purposes, in the manner and to the extent established by this Policy and applicable legislation.
p|Project website: **{{siteUrl}}**.
p|To send requests related to the processing of personal data, the data subject or their legal representative may contact the Operator:

list|by email: **{{contactsEmail}}**
by postal address: **{{contactsPostalAddress}}**

p|This Policy applies to personal data that the Operator receives directly from the data subject while using the Website, filling out questionnaires, registering for championships, events and workshops, participating in project activities, as well as during the subsequent moderation, publication and administration of the relevant content.

p|The Policy also applies to technical and service data generated by the information system when processing the relevant applications and questionnaires, including information necessary to ensure security, moderation and audit.
p|The Operator processes personal data based on the following principles:

list|processing is carried out for lawful and predetermined purposes
the volume of processed data corresponds to the stated purposes
only those categories of data that are necessary for the relevant purposes are used
personal data are not used for purposes not specified in this Policy
personal data are not sold
personal data are not used for targeted advertising
no profiling of data subjects is carried out
no automated decision-making that creates legal or similarly significant consequences for the data subject is carried out
marketing mailings are not carried out without appropriate consent
p|In cases where processing is based on consent, the relevant consent is provided electronically through the Website.

p|Consent is provided by the data subject performing the relevant action on a form, including ticking the box provided by the form confirming agreement with the terms of personal data processing and the relevant regulations.
p|Special requirements established by Section 4 of this Policy apply to the processing of data of minors.
p|**Personal data** — any information relating directly or indirectly to an identified or identifiable natural person.

p|**Operator** — a person who, independently or jointly with other persons, organises and/or carries out the processing of personal data, and also determines the purposes of processing, the composition of personal data and the actions performed with them.
p|Under this Policy, the Operator is **{{operatorName}}**.
p|**Data subject** — a natural person to whom the processed personal data relate.

p|**Processing of personal data** — any action or set of actions performed with personal data using automation tools or without them, including collection, recording, systematisation, accumulation, storage, clarification, modification, extraction, use, transfer, granting access, dissemination, depersonalisation, blocking, deletion and destruction.

p|**Consent to the processing of personal data** — a voluntary, specific, subject-related, informed and conscious expression of will by the data subject, provided in the cases and in the manner prescribed by legislation and this Policy.
p|**Depersonalisation** — actions as a result of which it becomes impossible to determine the ownership of personal data to a specific data subject without using additional information.
p|**Blocking** — temporary cessation of personal data processing, except for cases where processing is necessary to clarify personal data.

p|**Destruction** — actions as a result of which it becomes impossible to restore the content of personal data in the information system and/or as a result of which the physical media of personal data are destroyed.
p|**Cross-border transfer of personal data** — transfer of personal data to the territory of a foreign state to a state authority of a foreign state, a foreign natural or legal person.

p|**Authorised body** — a state body performing control and supervision functions in the field of personal data, including Roskomnadzor in cases provided for by the legislation of the Russian Federation.
p|**Cookies** — a small piece of data stored by a browser or other software on a user's device and used by the Website for the technical purposes provided for by this Policy.
p|**IP address** — a unique network address of a device or node in a computer network built using the IP protocol.
p|**Automated processing** — processing of personal data using computing and software tools.

p|**Moderation** — a check by an authorised person of the content and information provided by a user in order to decide on its approval, rejection, the need for changes or other further processing in accordance with the rules of the relevant section or activity.

p|The Operator processes personal data only for predetermined and specific purposes directly related to the functioning of Navykus, organising participation in events and championships, publishing profiles in the provided sections, moderation and ensuring the security of the Website.

table|No.;Processing purpose;Categories of personal data;Form/source|1;Registration for a championship / participation in a case championship;Identification, contact and profile data, portfolio files;Participant questionnaire (`sourceType=championship`)|2;Publishing a questionnaire in the "Find a Team" section after moderation;Identification, profile and contact data (Telegram/Email), country;Participant questionnaire (`sourceType=find-team / modal / home / about / activities`)|3;Registration for events and workshops;Identification, contact and profile data;Participant questionnaire (`sourceType=event / activities`)|4;Sending notifications about moderation status, championship information and deadlines;Name, email address;Automatically when the status changes or a provided action is performed|5;Content moderation, security and audit;Technical and service data (`sourceType`, `moderationStatus`, audit records and other service information);System processes|6;Performance of the championship participation agreement;Data necessary for the relevant participation;Questionnaire and consent to personal data processing

p|Personal data may be processed to accept a participant's questionnaire, register for the relevant championship, organise participation in a case championship, process the submitted materials and perform organisational actions related to participation.
p|Within the framework of this purpose, identification, contact and profile data and portfolio files may be processed to the extent established by this Policy.

subs.h: 3.4. Publishing a profile in the "Find a Team" section
blocks: p|After the provided moderation, questionnaire data may be published in the "Find a Team" section to the extent necessary for the stated purpose.
p|Publication is carried out only after the appropriate processing of the questionnaire and the adoption of the provided decision on its publication.
p|Published data include the identification and profile information provided for this purpose, contact data in the form of Telegram/Email and information about the country.
p|Personal data may be processed to register the data subject for events, workshops, online meetings and other Navykus project activities.
p|The Operator may send notifications directly related to the user's participation in the relevant activity, including:

list|notifications about moderation status
information about the championship
information about terms and deadlines
organisational notifications directly related to the relevant participation
p|Marketing mailings not directly related to the stated purposes are not among the processing purposes specified in this Policy.
p|Technical and service information is processed to:

list|carry out moderation
ensure the security of the Website
monitor the state of questionnaire processing
record actions with data
maintain an audit of content creation, modification and deletion operations
enable incident investigation and confirmation of actions of authorised persons

subs.h: 3.8. Purposes for which data are not used
blocks: p|The Operator **does not use** personal data for:

list|targeted advertising
profiling
automated decision-making
selling personal data
transferring personal data to third parties for marketing purposes
marketing mailings without appropriate consent
p|Google Analytics, Yandex.Metrica, advertising networks, social media pixels and other similar tools of analytical or advertising profiling are not used within the described system.

p|Personal data processing is carried out where there is a legal basis provided for by the legislation of the Russian Federation and, where applicable, by the personal data protection legislation of the relevant jurisdiction.

table|Type of processing;Basis under 152-FZ;Basis under GDPR|Acceptance of a questionnaire, moderation and profile publication;Consent, Art. 6 part 1 item 1;Art. 6(1)(a)|Registration for a championship and performance of contractual relations;Performance of a contract, Art. 6 part 1 item 2;Art. 6(1)(b)|Notifications about participation and status;Legitimate interest, Art. 6 part 1 item 5, and/or consent;Art. 6(1)(f) and/or Art. 6(1)(a)|Audit, security and protection of rights;Performance of a legal obligation, Art. 6 part 1 item 3, including requirements of 152-FZ Art. 18 and 19;Art. 6(1)(c)|Technical Cookies and recording of Cookie consent;Consent, Art. 9 of 152-FZ;ePrivacy / Art. 6(1)(a)

subs.h: 4.3. Consent to the processing of personal data
blocks: p|In cases where the basis is consent, the data subject provides it through the Website interface before the relevant processing begins or by performing a system-provided action confirming such consent.
p|The consent form must make it possible to identify its subject matter and the fact of providing consent.

p|In cases related to participation in a championship, processing may be carried out on the basis of the need to perform contractual relations between the data subject and the Operator to the extent that processing is necessary for the performance of the relevant obligations.

p|Technical and service data may be processed to the extent necessary to comply with statutory requirements, ensure the security of the information system, maintain audit and protect the rights and legitimate interests of the Operator and data subjects.

p|The Operator **does not process special categories of personal data** relating to information about race, nationality, political views, religious or philosophical beliefs, health, intimate life, genetic data and biometric personal data.
p|Age specified in a questionnaire as a numerical value is not considered by the Operator as a special category of personal data.
p|Navykus is aimed at users aged 10 to 22. In this regard, special requirements for providing consent apply to minors.
p|For users aged **10–13**, this Policy requires the consent of a legal representative.
p|For users aged **14–17**, the data subject's own consent applies. In this case, notification of parents or other legal representatives is recommended.
p|For users aged **18 and older**, consent is provided directly by the data subject independently.
p|These requirements are requirements of this Policy regardless of whether the relevant technical control mechanism is implemented directly in the Website code.
p|Personal data are processed by automated and manual methods.
p|In automated form, personal data are processed, in particular, through the following processes:

list|receiving questionnaire data via `POST /api/team-members`
writing data to the SQLite database (`payload.db`)
sending email notifications via Nodemailer
publishing the relevant content on the frontend after moderation
maintaining an audit of operations
p|Manual processing includes:

list|moderation of questionnaires in Payload Admin
approval of questionnaires
rejection of questionnaires
making necessary changes to data
exporting data at the request of the data subject
deleting data at the request of the data subject

table|Category;Fields;Required|Identification;`name`, `age`;Yes|Contact;`email`, `contact`, `contactType`, `country`, `city`;`city` — no (the rest — yes)|Profile;`shortBio`, `interests[]`, `skills[]`, `targetRoles[]`, `targetProject`, `whyLooking`;Partially|Files;`portfolioFiles[]`, `portfolioLink`;No|Technical/service;`sourceType`, `sourceId`, `sourceContext`, `tournamentId`, `moderationStatus`, `moderationComment`, `reviewedAt`, `isApproved`, `originalLanguage`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`;Automatically|Cookie / localStorage;`navykus.cookieConsent` with the value `accepted` or `dismissed`;Consent information only
p|The `portfolioFiles[]` field is intended for uploading portfolio files.
p|Files of the following types are allowed:

list|PDF
DOC
DOCX
JPG
PNG
WebP
p|The size of one file must not exceed **10 MB**. The maximum number of portfolio files is **5**.
p|The `portfolioLink` field may also be used.

p|Technical and service data include information automatically generated by the system to ensure functioning, moderation and audit, including `sourceType`, `sourceId`, `sourceContext`, `tournamentId`, `moderationStatus`, `moderationComment`, `reviewedAt`, `isApproved`, `originalLanguage`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt` and audit data.
p|The Website uses technical storage of the user's consent value in `localStorage` under the key:
p|`navykus.cookieConsent`
p|Possible values:

list|`accepted`
`dismissed`
p|Only necessary Cookies and technical storage related to consent and the administrator session are used.
p|Analytical and marketing Cookies are not used.
p|Personal data are stored for the period necessary to achieve the processing purposes, until consent is withdrawn or until the expiry of the statutory period.
p|In particular:

table|Category;Period|Questionnaires of approved participants;Until consent is withdrawn or 3 years of inactivity counted from the last login/update|Questionnaires of rejected participants and questionnaires under moderation;30 days after the moderator's decision, after which they are subject to deletion|Audit logs `AuditLogs`;At least 3 years|Cookie consent;Until the user clears `localStorage`
p|There is no automated deletion of data directly in the system code.
p|Data deletion is performed manually by a moderator in the administrative system or in connection with another basis provided for by the Policy.
p|General storage principle: personal data are stored until the processing purpose is achieved, consent is withdrawn or the statutory period expires.

p|In cases where temporary cessation of processing is necessary, the relevant data may be blocked or their status may be changed in the administrative system in accordance with the procedure for considering a data subject's request.

sections.title: 6. TRANSFER OF DATA TO THIRD PARTIES

blocks: p|The Operator does not transfer personal data to third parties for the purposes of selling data, targeted advertising or marketing profiling.
p|Individual technological components and infrastructure solutions directly related to the functioning of the system may be used during processing.

table|Sub-processor / component;Purpose;Processed data;Basis;Location;DPA/SCC|Payload CMS / SQLite (`payload.db`);Database storage;All questionnaire data;Contract;RF, locally on the Operator's server;Internal|Nodemailer / SMTP;Email notifications to moderator and user;Email, name, form data;Contract / legitimate interest;Depends on the SMTP provider specified in the environment;Signed|Payload Media / local storage `uploads/media`;Storage of portfolio files;Uploaded files;Contract;RF, locally;Internal
p|The main database of the system is stored in the `payload.db` file used by Payload CMS on the Operator's server.
p|All questionnaire data necessary for the stated processing purposes may be stored in this database.
p|To send system-provided email notifications, Nodemailer with an SMTP provider specified in the environment variables of the relevant infrastructure is used.
p|Depending on the SMTP provider settings, email data may be processed by the relevant SMTP provider to the extent necessary to deliver the notification.
p|Portfolio files are stored via Payload Media on the local disk in the `uploads/media` directory.

subs.h: 6.6. Services to which data are not transferred
blocks: p|Within the described system, personal data are not transferred to:

list|Google Analytics
Yandex.Metrica
social networks
advertising networks
payment gateways
CRM systems
CDNs with personalisation
marketing trackers
p|Transfer of personal data to state authorities is carried out only where there is a statutory basis and in the manner prescribed by law.
p|Such cases include, in particular, statutory requests of courts, Roskomnadzor, investigative bodies and other authorised state authorities.
p|The Operator takes organisational and technical measures to protect personal data from unlawful or accidental access, destruction, modification, blocking and other unlawful actions.
p|The measures applied correspond to the actually implemented mechanisms of the system.
p|Data transfer over the network is carried out using HTTPS and TLS version **1.2 or higher**.
p|The Payload JWT authentication mechanism is used for administrative access.
p|The JWT token is stored in:

list|an HttpOnly cookie
a Secure cookie
a cookie with the SameSite=Lax parameter
p|The token validity period is determined by the `PAYLOAD_TOKEN_EXPIRATION_SECONDS` parameter. The default value is **4 hours**.
p|After **5 failed login attempts**, access is blocked for **15 minutes**.
p|The administrative system uses a role-based access model, including the roles:

list|`admin`
`moderator`
p|Public submission of questionnaires is carried out via:
p|`POST /api/team-members`
p|A public request is processed with the forced setting of the relevant status:

list|`pending`
`false` for the publication flag
p|A public user is not granted direct read access to the `TeamMembers` collection.
p|The `express-rate-limit` request rate limiting mechanism is applied to the API.
p|This measure is used to reduce the risk of abuse of public API methods and automated submission of large numbers of requests.
p|A whitelist of allowed MIME types is applied when uploading files:

list|PDF
DOC
DOCX
JPG
PNG
WebP
p|Restrictions are also applied:

list|no more than 10 MB per file
no more than 5 portfolio files
p|Verification is carried out on both the client and server sides.
p|Payload's built-in validation is used to check the structure and valid values of data.
p|Raw SQL queries are not used in the described mechanism of the system.
p|The `AuditLogs` collection is used to control operations.
p|The following operations may be recorded in the audit:

list|creation
modification
deletion
p|For audit operations, the following is recorded, in particular:

list|who performed the action
when the action was performed
which data were changed
the state of the data before the change
the state of the data after the change
p|The `payload.db` database is stored on the Operator's server.
p|Encryption of data at rest is ensured at the operating system/disk level of the server.
p|Automated backup is not implemented directly in the system code.
p|Responsibility for backup belongs to the Operator.
p|The procedure for responding to information security incidents is documented in the Operator's internal documents.

p|A separate Data Protection Officer (DPO) has not been appointed due to the scale of the activity and the absence of processing of special categories of personal data, based on the described processing model.

p|The data subject has the rights provided for by the legislation of the Russian Federation and, where applicable, by the legislation of the relevant jurisdiction, including the rights provided for by the GDPR.
p|To exercise rights, a written request is sent by email to **{{contactsEmail}}** or by postal address **{{contactsPostalAddress}}**.
p|There is no self-service user portal for managing personal data in the system.
p|The data subject has the right to request information about the processed personal data.
p|To exercise this right, a request must be sent to **{{contactsEmail}}**.
p|After reviewing the request, the moderator may export the relevant data from Payload Admin in JSON format.
p|If inaccuracies are identified or personal data need to be updated, the data subject may send the relevant request to **{{contactsEmail}}**.
p|After confirming the request, the moderator may make the necessary changes in the administrative system.
p|The data subject has the right to request the deletion of personal data.
p|The request is sent to **{{contactsEmail}}**.
p|After processing the request, the moderator deletes the relevant document from the administrative system, including the provided cascading deletion of related Media files.
p|In cases provided for by law, the data subject has the right to demand restriction of personal data processing.
p|To exercise this right, a request is sent to **{{contactsEmail}}**.
p|In the administrative system, the relevant processing may be restricted by changing the status, including to:

list|`moderationStatus='rejected'`
`moderationStatus='needs_edit'`
p|In cases where this right applies, the data subject has the right to request personal data in a structured format.
p|Within the existing system, such provision is implemented through JSON export of data from the administrative panel.
p|The data subject has the right to withdraw the provided consent to the processing of personal data in cases where processing is carried out on the basis of consent.
p|To do this, a request must be sent to **{{contactsEmail}}**.
p|Within the existing implementation, withdrawal of consent is processed similarly to a data deletion request, unless otherwise required to continue processing on another legal basis.
p|Consent to technical Cookies may be associated with the `navykus.cookieConsent` value. The user clears the relevant value in `localStorage` themselves.
p|The data subject has the right to file a complaint with the authorised body, including Roskomnadzor, in the manner prescribed by the legislation of the Russian Federation.
p|The Operator's details and information about registration in the personal data operators register are specified in Section 9 of this Policy.
p|Upon receiving a request, the Operator reviews it and, where there are legal and technical grounds, performs the relevant actions in the administrative system.
p|The period for considering a request is **30 calendar days**, unless a different period is provided for by applicable legislation.
p|Entry in the personal data operators register:
p|**No. {{operatorRegistryNumber}} dated {{operatorRegistryDate}}**
p|Register information is available on the official Roskomnadzor resource:
p|https://pd.rkn.gov.ru/

list|**Email:** {{contactsEmail}}
**Postal address:** {{contactsPostalAddress}}
p|Website:
p|**{{siteUrl}}**
p|All questions, demands and requests related to personal data processing are sent to the Operator using the contact details provided.
p|To process a request, the Operator may request information necessary to identify the applicant and verify their authority, to the extent provided for by legislation.
p|The response period for a data subject's request is **30 calendar days**, unless a different period is expressly established by applicable legislation.
p|**The legislation of the Russian Federation** applies to this Policy and to the relations between the Operator and the data subject.
p|In cases where the GDPR requirements or other mandatory norms of the relevant jurisdiction apply to personal data processing, the Operator takes them into account to the extent provided for by law.
p|Before going to court, the data subject has the right to send the Operator a claim or another written request demanding voluntary settlement of the relevant issue.
p|The response period for a claim is **30 calendar days**.
p|If the dispute cannot be settled out of court, the dispute is resolved by the court in accordance with applicable legislation.

p|For relations governed by the legislation of the Russian Federation, the procedure for filing a claim established by the legislation of the Russian Federation applies, taking into account the rules of jurisdiction.
p|The Operator has the right to make changes to this Policy.
p|A new version comes into force from the moment of its publication on the Website, unless otherwise provided by the new version itself.
p|The current version date is indicated in the field:
p|**{{lastUpdated}}**

p|In the event of a significant change in the terms of personal data processing, information about such changes may be additionally communicated to users via a banner on the Website and/or email notification, if the relevant mechanism is implemented.
p|The Website includes a separate Cookie consent mechanism (`CookieConsent`).
p|Within the described system, only necessary technical Cookies related to:

list|the administrator session
storing information about user consent
p|Analytical and marketing Cookies are not used.
p|The Operator separately informs data subjects that automated deletion of personal data directly in the system's program code is not implemented.
p|Deletion is carried out manually by an authorised moderator in the administrative panel or in accordance with another basis provided for by this Policy.
p|This Policy is a public document and applies to all personal data processing relations falling within its scope.
p|Use of the Website, submission of questionnaires and provision of other information means familiarisation with this Policy in the relevant part.
p|If the data subject does not agree with the terms of personal data processing, they should stop using the relevant Website features and not provide data whose processing requires their consent.
p|**Last updated: {{lastUpdated}}**

tournaments.title: Navykus Global Case Cup: Sustainable Cities
tournaments.description: Developing innovative solutions to the urban challenges of the future. International jury, real cases from urbanists, architects and ecologists from all over the world.
tournaments.suitableFor: Schoolchildren in grades 8–11 who are passionate about ecology, urbanism and social innovation.
tournaments.format: Online (group stage, defense of projects via video conference)

tournaments.title: Future Tech Project Incubator
tournaments.description: An intensive program to launch your own startup or social project. Turn your idea into a minimum viable product (MVP) in three weeks with guidance from Silicon Valley trackers.
tournaments.suitableFor: Authors of ideas, aspiring programmers, designers and future entrepreneurs.
tournaments.format: Online (intensive workshops, traction maps, demo day)

tournaments.title: International Youth Debate & Policy Forum
tournaments.description: Global debate on the ethics of artificial intelligence and space exploration. Develop skills in argumentation and diplomatic correspondence in English and Russian.
tournaments.suitableFor: Students developing public speaking skills, humanities and international relations.

pillars.label: 01 / CHAMPIONSHIPS
pillars.title: Online championships
pillars.description: Large-scale international competitions in solving cases. Try yourself in solving real problems from industry leaders.

pillars.label: 02 / COMMUNITY
pillars.title: Community and Mentors
pillars.description: Space for matching and expert mentoring. Find teammates from all over the world and get direct contact with practitioners from top universities.

pillars.label: 03 / ACTIVITIES
pillars.title: Useful activities
pillars.description: Master classes, workshops, open lectures from experts. Continuous learning regardless of participation in tournaments.

experts.name: Dr. Mark Spielman
experts.role: Professor of Urban Studies at MIT
experts.description: 15+ years of research in the field of environmental technologies and automation of urban infrastructure. Mentor of the Sustainable Cities track.

experts.name: Alex Chen
experts.description: Founder of two EdTech startups. Helps students crystallize chaotic ideas into a clear, working prototype.

experts.name: Anna Sokolova
experts.description: Coordinator of global youth forums with the support of UNESCO. Teaches effective presentation and the art of debate.

scenarios.title: Participate in the championship
scenarios.who: Schoolchild 14–18 years old with or without an idea
scenarios.why: Wants to test his strength in solving cases, receive awards and certificates. Can submit a form to the talent database for matching for upcoming tournaments.

scenarios.title: Find a team
scenarios.who: Author of the idea or solo participant
scenarios.why: The author needs designers and developers to implement the MVP; a loner needs a strong team to join.

trustPoints.title: Global scale
trustPoints.description: Participants and mentors from more than 15 countries create a truly multicultural educational environment.

trustPoints.title: Real practical cases
trustPoints.description: No abstract tasks. All cases and programs were created in collaboration with existing businesses and scientific laboratories.

trustPoints.title: Direct contact with mentors
trustPoints.description: Live communication, regular feedback, debriefing and expert assessment are the key value of our programs.

trustPoints.title: Turnkey project work
trustPoints.description: From a hypothesis and search for a problem to the first working prototype and defense to potential investors.

trustPoints.title: Finding like-minded people
trustPoints.description: A reliable and supportive community of ambitious peers who motivate you to move forward.

activities.title: Workshop: How to create an MVP in 48 hours
activities.shortDescription: Learn to turn ideas into a working prototype using no-code tools and design thinking.
activities.fullDescription: A two-day intensive workshop where you will go through the full cycle of creating a minimum viable product: from idea generation to presentation. You will learn how to use Figma, Notion and modern no-code platforms for rapid prototyping. At the end, each participant will receive a ready-made template for their MVP and feedback from practicing product managers.
activities.who: Schoolchildren aged 12–18 interested in product development and startups
benefits: Ready-made MVP prototype of your own project
Skills in working with Figma and no-code tools
activities.prerequisites: Basic understanding of what MVP is. No experience required.

activities.title: Lecture: Artificial intelligence in education
activities.shortDescription: An expert from Stanford will tell you how AI is changing school education and what skills will be in demand.
activities.fullDescription: An open lecture from a guest speaker - a researcher in the field of EdTech and artificial intelligence. You will learn how machine learning is already personalizing the educational process, what ethical issues the introduction of AI in schools raises, and what schoolchildren need to do to remain in the ranks of those who control technology, and not vice versa. After the lecture there is a question and answer session.
benefits: An Expert Perspective from a Stanford Researcher

activities.title: Hackathon: Green technologies for the city
activities.shortDescription: Team hackathon to develop environmental solutions for smart cities.
activities.fullDescription: A 48-hour team hackathon in which teams of 2-5 people must design a green solution for urban infrastructure. You will work in Miro and Figma, consult with environmental mentors and present the final pitch to the jury. The best teams will receive an invitation to the Future Tech Project Incubator.
activities.who: Schoolchildren aged 14–19, passionate about ecology, IT and urbanism
benefits: Invitation to the incubator for the best
activities.prerequisites: Desire to work in a team. Any skill is welcome.

activities.title: Master class: Public speaking and pitching
activities.shortDescription: How to convince the jury of the value of your project in 5 minutes - from structure to presentation.
activities.fullDescription: A practical master class from a tracker who helped schoolchildren win international debates and pitch sessions. You will understand the structure of an ideal pitch, practice speaking in pairs and receive personal feedback. It is especially useful for those who are preparing to defend a project at a championship or want to develop public speaking skills.
activities.who: Schoolchildren aged 13–18, ready to defend projects
activities.prerequisites: It is advisable to have your own project or idea

activities.title: Team track: Design sprint for social projects
activities.shortDescription: A 5-day design sprint where teams create a social project from scratch.
activities.fullDescription: Intensive team program using the design sprint methodology: day 1 - understanding the problem, day 2 - generating ideas, day 3 - decision making, day 4 - prototyping, day 5 - testing and presentation. Each team will receive its own facilitator and will present the result to an expert jury. Ideal for those who want to try teamwork in a structured format.
activities.who: Schoolchildren aged 14–18, looking for a team or ready to form their own
benefits: Full design sprint cycle on a real project
activities.prerequisites: Desire to work in a team. No experience required.

activities.title: Online conference: Future of Skills 2025
activities.shortDescription: Three-day conference on key skills for generation Z.
activities.fullDescription: The largest online conference of the Navykus community: 3 days, 20+ speakers from MIT, YC, Sorbonne, UN. Topics: critical thinking, emotional intelligence, digital literacy, global citizenship. Every day there is a keynote speech, panel discussion and interactive session. The conference took place in December 2025 and brought together 800+ participants from 30 countries.
benefits: Recordings of all reports are available

activities.title: Project: Peer Mentoring Program
activities.shortDescription: Become a mentor for younger students or find your own mentor.
activities.fullDescription: The platform allows older schoolchildren (16–19 years old) to become mentors for younger students (12–15 years old) and help them with project activities, choosing areas of development and preparing for participation in championships. The program includes onboarding for mentors, regular meetings and coordinator support. For mentees, this is an opportunity to get a personal mentor from another country.
activities.date: Applications can be submitted until September 1, 2026
benefits: Menti: personal mentor from another country
activities.prerequisites: For mentors - experience of participation in Navykusa projects

activities.title: Workshop: Research Fundamentals
activities.shortDescription: How to conduct research, work with data, and write scientific articles for schoolchildren.
activities.fullDescription: A three-hour workshop on research methods relevant to schoolchildren: qualitative and quantitative methods, working with sources, basic statistics, citation ethics and the structure of a scientific article. The speaker is a university lecturer who specializes in working with school research projects. As a result, a practical task with feedback.

activities.title: Hackathon: Accessible Environment 2025
activities.shortDescription: Development of IT solutions for people with disabilities.
activities.fullDescription: The annual hackathon of the Navykus community, dedicated to the development of technological solutions to ensure an accessible environment. The teams worked on real-life issues of inclusion: navigation apps for the visually impaired, interfaces for people with motor impairments, game mechanics for neurodivergent children. The final defense took place with the participation of experts from international foundations.
activities.who: Schoolchildren 14–19 years old, developers, designers, activists
benefits: A real product for an inclusive environment

activities.title: Networking: Asian Youth Connect
activities.shortDescription: Meeting for participants from Asia - search for teams and exchange of experience.
activities.fullDescription: Specialized networking session for schoolchildren from Asia and neighboring regions. In 2 hours, participants get to know each other in a virtual speed-dating format, share ideas, and look for teammates for the upcoming championships. The language of communication is English. The coordinator helps form mixed international teams.
activities.who: Schoolchildren aged 13–18 from the Asian region
benefits: Search for a team for the championship
